Ash.fact: Ash buys three tamales from Pilar, paying from his left pocket in a ritualized, wordless transaction.
Ash arrives at the unofficial roadside shrine on his walk north.
Ash pours two fingers of filtered lake water into the ceramic cup at the shrine as an offering.
Ash says the names of the dead aloud — his grandmother's first, then three others — but deliberately omits a fourth name.
Ash recites his memorized route from Waukegan to Kenosha under his breath, performing his internal navigation ritual.
Ash stops reciting and lingers at the shrine four minutes longer than usual, his hand resting on the wooden board, unable to move on.
It is confirmed that there is a fourth name Ash chose not to say at the shrine.
Ash discovers the tamales are cold before he even lifts the cloth, confirming he arrived late or they were left long ago.
Ash eats the cold tamales standing, refusing to sit as a deliberate act of non-belonging.
Ash leaves offerings at the shrine and performs his forty-seventh marking ritual at a shrine between Waukegan and the Kenosha Crossing.
Ash recites a route from memory under his breath while eating, encoding waypoint knowledge as oral tradition.
A young stranger appears in the doorway holding an unidentified cloth-wrapped object, watching Ash without hiding or threatening.
Ash observes that the boy's scarification marks are incomplete — half a set, freshly keloid, suggesting an interrupted or unfinished rite.
The boy speaks a name at Ash — a name that has not been used in eleven years and that the boy should not know.
Ash watches the empty doorway and drops his hand from his synthetic eye.
Ash and Brisa walk north together without explanation.
Ash recites the Iron Bend checkpoint mnemonic under his breath while walking.
Brisa asks how long it took Ash to learn all the checkpoint mnemonics.
Ash reveals that someone taught him the northern routes and the particular habits of inspectors, without naming who.
Ash identifies the smell of the package under his coat as the interior of a lived-in building.
